summary: Approved all three ProxRR/FedRR cases: original Algorithm 1 and Algorithm 3 support the stated orders, observation timing and normalization, and all 84 numeric leaves agree with independently recomputed three-epoch trajectories.

cases.reason: All nine inner vectors and three epoch-end vectors agree. Permutations and differing curvatures are nontrivial, lambda1/lambda2 are active, and changing gamma_t changes both sample steps and the single epoch-end prox scale. Final iterate is (179411/462080,-2534889/2957312). Independently verified 6 observations / 24 numeric leaves; maximum absolute discrepancy from serialized expected numbers 1.18e-16.

Every nonlinear inner update and epoch-end prox agrees. A separately evaluated signed-label logistic gradient recovers the original {0,1} loss derivative. Thresholding produces exact zero in coordinate 2; the final vector is approximately (0.467873065086433843,0). Independently verified 6 observations / 24 numeric leaves; maximum absolute discrepancy from serialized expected numbers 6e-17.

Independent local passes and resets, first-sample states, endpoints, equal-device mean and final prox all agree. With N=5,M=2,gamma=1/8, alpha=5/16, threshold=1/32 and shrink denominator=37/32. Final vector is approximately (0.879447236474456103,0.665908238406412256). Independently verified 12 observations / 36 numeric leaves; maximum absolute discrepancy from serialized expected numbers 1.31e-16.
citations: PDF p.7 Eq.(13), zero padding and Algorithm 3 lines 4-9

scope_notes: Original source is the designated local paper.pdf; contract digest binds the exact frozen private contract. Allowed contract/derivation and schema were read, and neither frozen standards nor production code were modified. No adapter, implementation workspace, actual output, or standalone prior review file was read.
Approval certifies these finite tests as valid paper-grounded checks; passing them is not a guarantee of all implementation correctness.

Algorithm 1 on p.3 applies n unnormalized component-gradient steps followed by one prox with coefficient gamma_t*n. Its positive supplied gamma_t sequence may vary by epoch; the nonmonotone first test is an algorithm test and does not claim the theorem schedule in Eq.(11).

Algorithm 3 on p.7 permits unequal local sample counts, pads shorter local passes by zero functions, averages device endpoints with 1/M, and applies prox_(gamma*N/M R). The later equal-sample convergence assumptions do not invalidate this finite recurrence.

Logistic labels {0,1}, lack of intercept, objective normalization and elastic-net coefficients are explicit. The second coordinate is thresholded to zero at each logistic epoch end; the first coordinate remains nonzero. Given permutations specify conditional realizations, without testing uniform sampling or RNG conventions.

This validates only three-epoch full-precision ProxRR/FedRR traces at 1e-10 absolute and 1e-9 relative tolerances. It does not validate stochastic sampling distributions, Shuffle-Once, resampling, convergence, full empirical reproduction, or arbitrary lower-precision arithmetic.

Source-boundary disclosure: the permitted derive_contract.py unexpectedly contains an embedded prior-review prose string near its end, and part of that string was displayed during a code read. No standalone prior PAPER_REVIEW report was opened. The findings here are based on visually inspected original formula pages and new arithmetic; this incidental exposure means this review should not be represented as completely blind to all prior-review prose.
